Pulitzer Center Opens 2026 Global South Civil Society Microgrants of Up to $4,000

Pulitzer Center Opens 2026 Global South Civil Society Microgrants of Up to $4,000

Civil society organisations, grassroots groups, youth movements and community-based organisations across Africa and other parts of the Global South have an opportunity to secure funding under the Pulitzer Center Global South Civil Society Microgrants 2026.

The programme provides grants ranging from US$2,000 to US$4,000 for civic engagement projects that use Pulitzer Center-supported journalism to increase public understanding and encourage community action around important climate and environmental challenges.

Applications opened on 15 August 2026 and will close on 6 September 2026.

About the Opportunity

The Pulitzer Center is seeking proposals from civil society actors in the Global South that can transform journalism into meaningful community engagement.

Rather than funding new journalism or news reporting, the microgrant supports organisations to take existing Pulitzer Center-supported reporting and use it as a foundation for community education, dialogue, creative engagement and other activities capable of producing real-world impact.

For the 2026 cycle, projects must address one or more of three broad environmental themes: rainforests, oceans, and climate and labour.

The climate and labour component is particularly broad, covering issues such as gender, livelihoods, climate adaptation and community resilience.

Funding Available

Successful applicants can receive between US$2,000 and US$4,000.

The funding can support an existing initiative or help an organisation launch a new activity that meets the objectives of the programme.

Projects will generally be implemented for up to six months, with the main implementation period scheduled between October 2026 and March 2027.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is open to organisations and groups operating in the Global South, particularly Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia.

Eligible applicants include:

  • Civil society organisations;
  • Grassroots organisations;
  • Community educators;
  • Youth movements;
  • Community-led movements;
  • Civic coalitions; and
  • Other groups working at the intersection of journalism, civic rights and active citizenship.

Applicants are expected to have previous experience implementing civic engagement activities and demonstrate the capacity to manage an international microgrant.

Organisations should also have relevant experience in the environmental issue addressed by their proposed project.

What Types of Projects Can Be Supported?

Projects must meaningfully use at least one piece of journalism supported by the Pulitzer Center.

Activities could include community knowledge-sharing sessions, public dialogues, community organising, digital awareness campaigns, public performances and other creative approaches.

The fund is particularly interested in projects that improve awareness and critical thinking, amplify perspectives of communities affected by environmental problems, contribute to better-informed dialogue and equip communities with information they can use to take action.

For example, an African NGO working with women whose livelihoods are being affected by climate change could identify relevant Pulitzer Center reporting on climate and labour and use it during community dialogues, workshops and public engagement activities.

What the Grant Does Not Support

Applicants should understand that this is not a journalism reporting grant.

Projects primarily intended to produce journalism are outside the scope of the programme.

The grant also excludes projects that do not use Pulitzer Center-supported reporting, direct lobbying or advocacy targeting parliamentary processes, activities supporting political candidates or parties, and for-profit projects.

Application Requirements

Applicants will be required to submit information including a project description of no more than 400 words, target audience and intended impact, implementation methodology, timeline and proposed budget.

The application also requires the CV of the lead applicant and a recommendation letter from a department head or director of the applicant’s organisation or workplace.

Where activities involve knowledge exchange with Indigenous peoples or traditional communities, evidence of community consent may also be required.

Key Dates

Application opens: 15 August 2026
Application deadline: 6 September 2026
Selection announcement: Mid-September 2026
Onboarding: October 2026
Implementation: October 2026–March 2027
Project closure: Early March 2027

How to Apply

Interested organisations should carefully review the official guidelines, identify an eligible Pulitzer Center-supported story relevant to their proposed intervention, prepare their project concept and budget, and submit the application before the deadline.

Applications are available in English, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Bahasa Indonesia.
